items.q: Scores on a memory test are normally distributed with a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 10. What is the z score of a student who scored 70?

why.correct: $z = \frac{70 - 50}{10} = \frac{20}{10} = 2$: two standard deviations above the mean.

mistakes.why: 20 is how many points above the mean the score is. Divide by the standard deviation, 10.
The score is above the mean, so z is positive.

items.q: On a test with a mean of 80 and a standard deviation of 5, what is the z score of a score of 75?

why.correct: $z = \frac{75 - 80}{5} = \frac{-5}{5} = -1$: one standard deviation below the mean.

mistakes.why: The score is below the mean, so z is negative.
-5 is the distance in points. Divide by the standard deviation, 5.

items.q: By the 68-95-99.7 rule, what percent of scores in a normal distribution fall within two standard deviations of the mean?

mistakes.why: 47.5% is one side only. Add both sides of the mean.
68% is within one standard deviation. Two standard deviations hold 95%.

items.q: In a normal distribution, what percent of scores fall more than one standard deviation above the mean?

why.correct: Half the scores are above the mean (50%), and 34% are between the mean and $z = 1$. So $50 - 34 = 16\%$ are above $z = 1$.

mistakes.why: 34% lies between the mean and one SD above it. Above one SD is what is left of the upper half: 50 - 34.
32% lies outside one SD on both sides together. Above it is half of that.

items.q: A student’s score is one standard deviation above the mean of a normal distribution. By the 68-95-99.7 rule, what is the student’s percentile rank?

why.correct: Percent below $z = 1$: the lower half (50%) plus 34% between the mean and $z = 1$, so 84. The student is at the 84th percentile.

mistakes.why: 34% is only the band between the mean and one SD. Add the 50% below the mean.
68% lies within one SD on both sides; it is not the percent below a score.

items.q: Maya scored at the 90th percentile on a reading test. What does that mean?
options: She scored higher than about 90% of test takers
She answered about 90% of the test questions correctly
Her score is 90 points above the mean
She is in the top 90% of the test takers

why.correct: A percentile rank is the percent of scores that fall below a given score. Percent correct is a different number.
options: Right: a percentile rank is the percent of scores below hers.
Percentile is about rank among test takers, not the percent correct.
A percentile is a rank, not a distance in points.
The top 90% would include nearly everyone; she is in the top 10%.

items.q: Ana scored 72 on a biology test (mean 60, standard deviation 6) and 85 on a history test (mean 80, standard deviation 10). On which test did she do better compared with the other students?
options: History, because 85 is a higher raw score
Biology, where her z score is +2
History, where her z score is +5
Equally well, since she was above the mean both times

why.correct: A z score puts scores from different tests on the same scale: standard deviations from each test’s own mean.
options: Raw scores on different tests cannot be compared directly; compare z scores.
Right: z = (72 - 60)/6 = 2 in biology, but (85 - 80)/10 = 0.5 in history.
85 - 80 = 5 points, but dividing by the SD of 10 gives z = 0.5.
She was above both means, but by 2 SDs in biology and only 0.5 SD in history.

items.q: By the 68-95-99.7 rule, what percent of test takers scored between 85 and 115?

why.correct: 85 and 115 are one standard deviation below and above the mean of 100: $34 + 34 = 68\%$.

mistakes.why: 34% is one side only, 100 to 115. Add 85 to 100.
95% is within two standard deviations, 70 to 130.

items.q: What percent of test takers scored above 130?

why.correct: 130 is two standard deviations above the mean. Above it: $2.35 + 0.15 = 2.5\%$.

mistakes.why: 5% is outside two SDs on both sides together. Above 130 is only the upper half of that.
13.5% is the band from 115 to 130, below 130 rather than above it.

items.q: A student scored 70. What is that score’s z score?

mistakes.why: 70 is below the mean of 100, so z is negative.
-30 is the distance in points. Divide by the SD, 15.

items.q: About what percentile rank does a score of 115 have?
options: The 34th percentile
The 68th percentile
The 84th percentile
The 115th percentile

why.correct: Percentile rank is the percent of scores below a score: $50 + 34 = 84$.
options: 34% is the band from 100 to 115, not the percent below 115.
68% lies between 85 and 115; it is not the percent below 115.
Right: 50% below the mean plus 34% from 100 to 115.
Percentile ranks run from 0 to 100; 115 is the score.

items.q: Two students scored 55 and 145. What do these scores have in common?
options: Each is at the 50th percentile of the curve
Each has a z score of +3 on this test
Each is shared by about 34% of test takers
Each is three SDs from the mean

why.correct: Both are three standard deviations (45 points) from the mean of 100, one below and one above. Only about 0.3% of scores are that far out.
options: The 50th percentile is the mean, 100.
Only 145 has z = +3; 55 has z = -3.
34% is the band between the mean and one SD.
Right: 100 - 45 = 55 and 100 + 45 = 145, with an SD of 15.

items.q: By the 68-95-99.7 rule, what percent of the teens slept between 8 and 9 hours?

why.correct: 8 hours is one standard deviation above the mean and 9 hours is two. The band between them holds $13.5\%$.

mistakes.why: 34% is the band next to the mean, 7 to 8 hours. The question asks about the next band out, 8 to 9.
47.5% is everything from the mean to two SDs above it, 7 to 9 hours. Leave out the 34% from 7 to 8.

items.q: A teen slept 5 hours. By the 68-95-99.7 rule, what is this teen’s percentile rank?

why.correct: 5 hours is two standard deviations below the mean. Below it lies $2.35 + 0.15 = 2.5\%$ of the teens, so the percentile rank is 2.5.

mistakes.why: 97.5 is the percentile rank two SDs above the mean, at 9 hours. 5 hours is two SDs below.
5% lies outside two SDs on both sides together. Below 5 hours is only the lower half of that.
47.5% is the share between 5 and 7 hours. A percentile rank is the percent below the score.

items.q: Which statement about the mean, median and mode of this distribution is correct?
options: The mean is 7 hours, but the median is lower
All three are 7 hours, at the peak of the curve
The mode is 7 hours, but the mean is higher
They cannot be found from a curve like this one

why.correct: A normal curve is symmetric, so the mean, the median and the mode all sit at the same point, the peak in the middle: 7 hours.
options: The curve is symmetric, so half the teens are below 7 hours and the median equals the mean.
Right: in a symmetric, bell-shaped distribution the three measures are equal.
The mean would be pulled above the mode only if the curve had a long tail to the right.
The peak of a normal curve marks all three, so they can be read from it.

items.q: Jon answered 60% of the questions on a very hard exam correctly, and his score report says he is at the 92nd percentile. How can both be true?
options: He outscored 92% of test takers while missing 40% of the items
The report is wrong: 60% correct must be the 60th percentile
He answered 92% of the hardest questions correctly
He scored two standard deviations above the mean of the exam

why.correct: A percentile rank is the percent of scores below a score, not the percent of questions right. On a very hard exam, 60% correct can beat almost everyone.
options: Right: percentile rank compares him with the other test takers.
A percentile is not the percent of questions right. It depends on how everyone else scored.
A percentile rank says nothing about which questions he got right.
Two standard deviations above the mean is about the 97.5th percentile, and the report says 92nd.
